req.title: DELETE is idempotent
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 on second and subsequent DELETE calls for the same playerId.

doc.reasoning: R-PLAYER-030 requires DELETE /players/squadnumber/{squad_number} to be idempotent: the first call on an existing player must return HTTP 204, and every subsequent call for the same squad number must return HTTP 404. The test suite covers: (1) positive/STC — full state transition from EXISTS→DELETED→NOT_FOUND across two sequential DELETEs; (2) negative/NEG — DELETE on a squad number that never existed returns 404 immediately; (3) boundary/BVA — the exact transition point between the 1st call (204) and 2nd call (404) is asserted with exact status codes to catch off-by-one and operator-flip mutations; (4) DT — a third DELETE after the second also returns 404, confirming idempotency holds beyond the second call; (5) EP — a mid-range squad number (squad 10) exercises the normal equivalence class. All assertions use exact integer status codes to kill constant-mutation and comparison-mutation operators.

tests.name: test_delete_idempotent_first_call_204_second_call_404
preconditions: Player with squadNumber=5 exists in the database (Vivaan Nair, id=2b515093-76be-4c72-98de-729c368f7ddb)
expected: First DELETE returns HTTP 204 No Content
Second DELETE returns HTTP 404 Not Found
trace: R-PLAYER-030: system shall respond with HTTP 404 on second and subsequent DELETE calls for the same playerId
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_delete_idempotent_first_call_204_second_call_404():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r1 = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/5')
    assert r1.status_code == 204
    r2 = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/5')
    assert r2.status_code == 404

BVA: boundary is the transition from call 1 (204) to call 2 (404)

tests.name: test_delete_idempotent_does_not_affect_other_players
actions: Assert squad_number in GET response is exactly 21
expected: DELETE of squad 20 is idempotent (204 then 404)
Squad 21 is unaffected and returns 200 with correct squad_number
trace: R-PLAYER-030: idempotency is scoped to the deleted playerId only
EP: normal equivalence class — mid-range squad numbers
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_delete_idempotent_does_not_affect_other_players():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r1 = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/20')
    assert r1.status_code == 204
    r2 = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/20')
    assert r2.status_code == 404
    r3 = client.get('/players/squadnumber/21')
    assert r3.status_code == 200
    body = r3.json()
    assert body['squadNumber'] == 21
    assert body['firstName'] == 'Rahul'
    assert body['lastName'] == 'Banerjee'

tests.name: test_delete_idempotent_response_body_on_404
actions: Send DELETE /players/squadnumber/26 (first call) — expect 204 with no body
Assert second response status is exactly 404
Assert second response is not 204 and not 500
expected: 404 response status code is exactly 404, not any other 4xx
trace: R-PLAYER-030: HTTP 404 specifically (not generic 4xx) on second DELETE
NEG: negative path — deleted resource must yield 404 not 410 or 400
tests.executable:
from main import app
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient

def test_delete_idempotent_response_body_on_404():
    client = TestClient(app)
    r1 = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/26')
    assert r1.status_code == 204
    r2 = client.delete('/players/squadnumber/26')
    assert r2.status_code == 404
    assert r2.status_code != 204
    assert r2.status_code != 500
    assert r2.status_code != 400
    assert r2.status_code != 410
